title: Retro-ingest Orchestrator: tenant-aware telemetry backfill with cost-aware throttling
creator: Aisha Kumar
description: Build a reusable orchestration service to perform large-scale telemetry retro-ingests (backfills and replays) that are tenant-aware, idempotent, and cost-throttled. This service should support: tenant bandwidth fencing, resumeable checkpointed windows, schema-versioned transforms, and tight observability so we can run corrective reprocesses without impacting real-time pipelines. The orchestrator will coordinate workers that read historical blobs from object storage, apply migration transforms, and materialize outputs into our analytics warehouse and metrics endpoints. It must integrate with existing RBAC, rate-limit quotas, and the Console's cost dashboards.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Orchestrator can run a full-tenant backfill for a ~30-day window and resume from a checkpoint after a simulated failure without duplicating outputs. 2) Supports per-tenant throughput caps and enforces a global cost budget, exposing live budget consumption to Console. 3) Transform step supports schema upgrade hooks and a tested fallback that routes problematic rows to quarantine. 4) End-to-end integration test that validates output parity within acceptable fuzz (<= 0.1% diff) versus golden baseline for a sampled tenant. 5) Operational runbook and Grafana dashboard linked in the ticket.
technical_notes:
- Orchestrator design: coordinator service issues windowed work units (time-range + tenant + resume token) and persists checkpoint manifests to S3 with strong consistency via transactional metadata table.
- Worker model: stateless workers read manifests and process streams in parallel. Each worker writes idempotent commit markers to prevent double-apply.
- Throttling: implement token-bucket per-tenant in coordinator with a cost translator that maps CPU/IO token consumption to dollars based on current pricing model.
- Schema migration: use pluggable transform chain; transforms expose schema version and reconciliation rules. On transform error route to quarantine bucket and emit structured annotation to telemetry.
- Idempotence: use deterministic output keys (tenant, window-start, source-offset-hash) and atomic rename semantics for finalization.
- Observability: meters for windows processed/sec, bytes read, cost-consumed, quarantine-rate, resume-counts; traceable span per-window.
- Safety: coordinator enforces conservative concurrency by default; policy flags allow burst-for-critical-customer replays.
- Trade-offs: choosing S3-manifest + metadata table gives lower runtime coupling vs using distributed checkpoint store; cost is eventual consistency edge cases handled via idempotent commits.
rollout_plan: Alpha: run orchestration against a synthetic dataset in staging and verify checkpoint/resume logic (2 weeks). Beta: enable limited production runs for non-critical tenants under a protective budget and observability (3 weeks). GA: expose UI in Console for scheduling backfills with RBAC and tenant-budget controls; enable programmatic API. Monitor cost and quarantine rates for two weeks before enabling for all tenants.
test_plan: Unit tests for manifest generation, resume token arithmetic, and transform chain. Integration test harness simulating worker failures, network partitions, and partial writes. Canary run using a single low-volume tenant with golden baseline comparison. Load test: run a 30-day synthetic backfill in staging to validate throughput, checkpoint stability, and cost accounting.
